items.q: Pink needle like Auer rods within blasts establish which lineage?
items.exp: Auer rods are crystallised myeloperoxidase in myeloblasts, proving myeloid lineage. Multiple rods in faggot cells characterise acute promyelocytic leukaemia.
r: Incorrect. Lymphoblasts lack Auer rods and express TdT.
Correct. Auer rods prove myeloid blasts.
Incorrect. Erythroid leukaemia is rare and not defined by rods.
Incorrect. Megakaryoblasts need platelet markers, not rods.
items.kp: Auer rods equal myeloid. Faggot cells equal promyelocytic.

items.q: Suspected acute promyelocytic leukaemia with DIC needs which immediate action?
o: Wait for cytogenetics before any therapy
Start all trans retinoic acid immediately with coagulation support
items.exp: ATRA must start on clinical suspicion because early haemorrhagic death precedes genetic confirmation. It differentiates promyelocytes while blood products support coagulopathy.
r: Incorrect. Waiting risks fatal bleeding.
Correct. Immediate ATRA plus support saves lives.
Incorrect. Cytoreduction alone misses differentiation therapy.
Incorrect. Folate has no role in this emergency.
items.kp: Suspect promyelocytic leukaemia, give ATRA now, confirm later.

items.q: The t(15;17) translocation creates which fusion driving promyelocytic leukaemia?
items.exp: t(15;17) fuses PML with the retinoic acid receptor alpha gene, blocking differentiation that pharmacological retinoic acid overcomes. BCR ABL1 defines chronic myeloid leukaemia instead.
r: Incorrect. BCR ABL1 defines CML and some ALL.
Correct. PML RARA drives promyelocytic leukaemia.
Incorrect. That fusion causes a core binding factor AML.
Incorrect. KMT2A lesions affect infant leukaemias.
items.kp: 15;17 means PML RARA means ATRA responsive.

items.q: Tumour lysis syndrome biochemistry is which combination?
o: High potassium, high phosphate, high urate, low calcium
Low potassium, low phosphate, low urate
High calcium with low phosphate only
items.exp: Cell breakdown releases intracellular potassium, phosphate and nucleic acids converted to uric acid, while phosphate binds calcium and lowers it. Kidney injury follows crystal deposition.
r: Correct. High K, high phosphate, high urate, low calcium.
Incorrect. Intracellular contents rise, not fall.
Incorrect. Calcium falls in tumour lysis, not rises.
Incorrect. Sodium is not the defining ion.
items.kp: Lysis labs: everything up except calcium down.

items.q: Commonest malignancy of childhood presenting with marrow failure and lymphadenopathy is what?
items.exp: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia peaks in young children and is the commonest childhood cancer, presenting with marrow failure, nodes and organ enlargement. Early response and genetics stratify cure.
r: Incorrect. AML dominates in older adults.
Correct. ALL is the commonest childhood cancer.
Incorrect. Neuroblastoma is a solid tumour of early childhood.
Incorrect. Hodgkin affects older children and young adults with nodes.
items.kp: Childhood leukaemia default answer is ALL.

items.q: Gum hypertrophy and skin infiltration (leukaemia cutis) most suggest which AML subtype tendency?
items.exp: Monocytic lineage acute myeloid leukaemia infiltrates gums, skin and meninges characteristically. Promyelocytic disease instead presents with coagulopathy and Auer packed cells.
r: Incorrect. Promyelocytic disease presents with DIC and faggot cells.
Correct. Monocytic AML infiltrates gums and skin.
Incorrect. Erythroid disease is marrow predominant.
Incorrect. Megakaryoblastic disease associates with Down syndrome in children.
items.kp: Swollen gums in AML means monocytic lineage.

items.q: Rasburicase prevents tumour lysis kidney injury by which action?
o: Converting uric acid to soluble allantoin
items.exp: Rasburicase enzymatically converts uric acid to highly soluble allantoin, rapidly lowering urate in high burden disease. Allopurinol only prevents new urate formation and works slower.
r: Incorrect. It does not act on potassium.
Correct. It degrades uric acid to allantoin.
Incorrect. Phosphate needs hydration and binders separately.
Incorrect. Calcium is managed by treating phosphate and lysis.
items.kp: Rasburicase destroys urate; allopurinol prevents its birth.

items.q: A leukemoid reaction differs from leukaemia by which feature?
o: Toxic granulation with high alkaline phosphatase and no blasts clone
items.exp: Severe infection drives leukemoid reactions with mature neutrophils, toxic granulation, Dohle bodies and high leukocyte alkaline phosphatase, without a clonal blast population.
r: Incorrect. Both can show very high counts.
Correct. Mature toxic change without clone means reaction.
Incorrect. Anaemia occurs in both settings.
Incorrect. Fever accompanies infection and leukaemia alike.
items.kp: Blasts and clonality separate leukaemia from reaction.

items.q: Why does ALL therapy include central nervous system prophylaxis?
o: Meninges shelter blasts from systemic drugs causing relapse
Intrathecal therapy replaces all systemic therapy
items.exp: The blood brain barrier shelters meningeal blasts from systemic chemotherapy, so intrathecal therapy and selected systemic agents prevent nervous system relapse.
r: Incorrect. Meningeal seeding is well recognised.
Correct. Sanctuary site prophylaxis prevents relapse.
Incorrect. Marrow needs full systemic therapy.
Incorrect. Intrathecal therapy supplements, never replaces, systemic treatment.
items.kp: Sanctuary sites need their own prophylaxis in ALL.

items.q: Down syndrome children have increased risk of which leukaemia pattern?
o: Transient abnormal myelopoiesis and megakaryoblastic AML
items.exp: Trisomy 21 with GATA1 mutations causes transient abnormal myelopoiesis in newborns and later megakaryoblastic acute myeloid leukaemia, plus increased ALL risk.
r: Incorrect. CML is not the characteristic association.
Correct. GATA1 related megakaryoblastic disease is characteristic.
Incorrect. Hairy cell disease affects older adults.
Incorrect. Adult T cell disease follows HTLV 1 infection.
items.kp: Down plus newborn blasts: think GATA1 transient myelopoiesis.
